articles.title: Rassie Erasmus banned for six matches over ‘match-fixing’ diatribe after France defeat
articles.summary: Springboks’ coach made contentious remarks in tirade. Misses Nations Championship finals at Twickenham. Rassie Erasmus has been banned for six international matches with immediate effect by World Rugby after an investigation into his remarkable rant on Monday in which he questioned whether…
body: The global governing body has moved swiftly with a disciplinary panel determining “that the threshold for serious misconduct had been met” by Erasmus, who also took aim at the standard of refereeing in the Nations Championship, suggesting a bias towards the northern hemisphere.

Erasmus will be forced to sit out South Africa’s clash with Ireland on Saturday as well as the Springboks’ match on finals weekend. It is likely to expire at some point during next year’s Rugby Championship, meaning it will not affect South Africa’s defence of their World Cup title. In 2021, Erasmus was handed a 10-and-a-half month ban for his verbal attack on the Australian referee Nic Berry during the British & Irish Lions series. If a similar ban been introduced this time he would have missed the Springboks’ entire World Cup warm-up campaign.

South Africa Rugby has exercised its right to request a full misconduct hearing, issuing a statement to outline how it had “requested an opportunity for its coach to contextualize his comments and assure the panel that it was not his intention to allege that any match official had acted with ulterior motives”.

articles.title: Wayne Rooney says he contemplated taking own life during playing career
articles.summary: Former England footballer reveals that the issues he faced occurred at the height of his Manchester United career. Wayne Rooney has revealed there was a period in his Manchester United career where he contemplated taking his own life.
body: He said he would spend two days at a time drinking at home and, he told the Life At The Midpoint with Gabby Logan podcast, at his lowest point considered taking his own life. “I can look back and say I was selfish, but I knew I was going through something which I was really struggling to deal with,” Rooney said. “Then I didn’t want Kai seeing me like that, so that’s why I’d hide away as well.

“I got to a place where you’re contemplating suicide. You just didn’t want to be around anyone. I didn’t want to be see people in the streets. I didn’t want to go into shops. I was always comfortable on a football pitch, but everything else [I] really struggled with it.”

articles.title: Rising star Fils earns first ATP Finals win
articles.summary: Rising star Arthur Fils claims his first career win at the ATP Finals by battling to a comeback victory over Rafael Jodar to remain in contention in Turin.
body: Fils, 22, beat 20-year-old Jodar 4-6 6-2 6-2 to become the first Frenchman to record an ATP Finals victory since Jo-Wilfried Tsonga in 2011.

It was the youngest match by combined age at the season-ending tournament - which features the eight top-performing men - since a 21-year-old Novak Djokovic defeated a 20-year-old Juan Martin del Potro in 2008.
Fils has risen to a career-high ranking of seventh in the world during a season in which he became the youngest French ATP Masters 1000 champion in Cincinnati.
All four debutants at this year's tournament lost their opening match, with Fils beaten by American third seed Ben Shelton and Spain's Jodar losing to Alexander Zverev in the John McEnroe Group.

articles.title: Peter Storey, Arsenal Double winner and England international, dies aged 81
articles.summary: Storey made 501 appearances for Arsenal from 1965. He got 19 England caps and finished career at Fulham. Arsenal have paid tribute to Peter Storey, a key member of their 1971 Double-winning team, after the death of the former England midfielder at the age of 81.
body: Storey was part of the Bertie Mee team that secured the First Division title and FA Cup in a season that remains one of the most celebrated in Arsenal’s history and played 501 times for the club. That places him eighth on their appearances list.
Storey, who represented England on 19 occasions from 1971-73, earned respect for his uncompromising approach and versatility, also featuring at right-back.

Storey died in hospital after a short illness, surrounded by his family. Arsenal said: “Everyone at Arsenal is deeply saddened by the passing of 1970-71 Double winner Peter Storey. All our thoughts are with his family and loved ones at this incredibly sad time.”

Born in Surrey, Storey began his career at Arsenal and made his debut shortly after his 20th birthday in 1965. He is fondly remembered by the club’s fans for scoring a stoppage-time penalty in the 1971 FA Cup semi-final against Stoke that forced a replay and kept the Double dream alive.

articles.title: Tiger Woods to make golf return after two years at Hero World Challenge
articles.summary: Former world No 1 last competed at the Open in 2024. Woods was arrested on DUI charge earlier this year. Tiger Woods will make ⁠his long-awaited return to competitive golf at the Hero World Challenge next month at the unofficial event he hosts in the Bahamas.
body: His decision was posted on Instagram, with Woods joining the 20-man field along with Rickie Fowler and 2019 US Open champion Gary Woodland. The Hero World Challenge takes place in New Providence, Bahamas, from 3 to 6 December.

Woods last competed in the 2024 British Open at Royal Troon, where he missed the cut in his last year playing all four majors. He also played the 36-hole PNC Championship with his son, where he could ride in a cart.

Woods ruptured his achilles tendon in February 2025 and missed the entire year. As he was starting to practise this March, he was arrested on a DUI charge. Soon after he stepped away from golf altogether in order to be treated at a rehabilitation facility in Zurich.
Woods described himself as “feeling better” in a recent interview with Sirius XM, adding that he had been “training quite a bit.”

articles.title: Senegal become first side to book Afcon 2027 spot
articles.summary: Senegal become the first side to qualify for the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations, while Egypt miss the chance to join them and Nigeria suffer another setback.
body: Senegal became the first side to qualify for the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations (Afcon) after Mozambique secured a 1-0 win away against Ethiopia.
That result means the Teranga Lions, who beat Sudan 4-2 on Monday, are guaranteed a top-two finish in Group J with two rounds of fixtures to play.
Eight more sides, including Morocco, Cameroon and Ivory Coast, could join Patrick Vieira's side in booking a spot at next year's finals as the fourth round of fixtures culminates on Tuesday.
Egypt could have qualified with an away win over Malawi but were held to a goalless draw after an inspired second-half showing from Flames goalkeeper George Chikooka.

articles.title: Springboks boss Erasmus given six-game ban
articles.summary: South Africa head coach Rassie Erasmus has been suspended for six international matches with immediate effect, following the extraordinary comments he made about the officiating of his side’s 21-19 defeat to France.
body: SA Rugby has requested a full hearing in response to the sanction.

Erasmus delivered an outspoken press conference on Monday, during which he suggested officials had missed 17 illegal tackles against his side during the match at the Stade de France. He went as far as questioning whether "manipulation" of the result was behind why those incidents were not picked up.

World Rugby confirmed they had reviewed the comments, and an independent panel had imposed the ban under World Rugby's match official abuse sanction process, which was introduced in July in an attempt to reduce the levels of abuse received by officials by sanctioning comments deemed to have been made with a view to undermining confidence in officials.

A statement from World Rugby said: "The panel determined that the comments suggest that match officials acted with bias/prejudice or deliberately influenced the outcome of a match, and when the conduct is considered as a whole a reasonable person would conclude that the conduct constituted an unacceptable attack on the credibility and competence of the match officials.

articles.title: Mercedes set to run ADUO engine upgrade in Las Vegas with one driver
articles.summary: World champions Mercedes will bring their ADUO turbocharger upgrade to this weekend's Las Vegas Grand Prix, although George Russell will not use it to avoid having to take another grid penalty in his bid for second place in the Drivers' Championship.
body: Mercedes in June were granted one chance to upgrade their power unit this season after being found to be between two and four per cent behind the best-performing internal combustion engine - which was unexpectedly judged to be Red Bull's - by the FIA in the year's first ADUO (Additional Development and Upgrade Opportunities) assessment window.

While rivals Ferrari, Audi and Honda, who were all found to be more than four per cent behind Red Bull's output and granted two upgrade opportunities, have all updated their respective power units at least once since, Mercedes had continued to keep their sole update chance in reserve.
But that ADUO upgrade - which Mercedes have focused on their power unit's turbo - is now ready to use in Las Vegas, although the team have played down the significance of its likely performance.

Given that expectation, Mercedes say that only world champion Kimi Antonelli is expected to use it given the Italian, who clinched the drivers' title two races ago in Mexico, remains one turbo within his penalty-free allowance of the season.

articles.title: Who is NFL MVP favourite? 'He’s head and shoulders above the rest’
articles.summary: Who is leading the NFL's MVP race? Sky Sports' Neil Reynolds explores his frontrunners heading into the second half of the 2026 season on the road to Super Bowl LXI...
body: When I was asked to write a column about the frontrunners for the Most Valuable Player award in the NFL this season, I thought it might be quite fun to compile such a list and look at the leading players in the NFL.

But the reality is this could be a one paragraph feature, because I believe Joe Burrow of the Cincinnati Bengals is head and shoulders above what is also a very good group looking for that prestigious prize.
Burrow is enjoying the form of his life for the 7-2 Cincinnati Bengals, as he demonstrated on Sunday Night Football, delivering a devastating performance to dismantle the Pittsburgh Steelers.

Burrow threw for over 300 yards and three touchdowns in the first half alone before Cincinnati called off the dogs in a 38-18 win. Burrow ended that game with more than 400 passing yards, four touchdowns, no interceptions, and the praise from future Hall of Famer Aaron Rodgers ringing in his ears as he said 'you put on a clinic kid'.

articles.title: Arsenal double winner Peter Storey dies aged 81 as tributes paid to England legend
articles.summary: Former England and Arsenal legend Peter Storey has passed away at the age of 81. Storey was an instrumental figure in the Gunners' historic 1971 double-winning squad, playing a pivotal role in securing both the First Division championship and the FA Cup under manager Bertie Mee.
body: Arsenal confirmed the news of his passing on Tuesday, stating via The Mirror: "Everyone at Arsenal is deeply saddened by the passing of 1970-71 Double winner Peter Storey. All our thoughts are with his family and loved ones at this incredibly sad time."

Storey made 501 appearances for Arsenal over 15 years and remains eighth on the club's all-time list. The North London club intends to honor the club icon ahead of their UEFA Champions League fixture against Borussia Dortmund.
Renowned for his versatility, the midfielder earned 19 caps for England under the legendary Alf Ramsey. His international debut came in 1971 in a commanding 3-0 victory over Greece at Wembley.
Storey's journey in soccer began when he joined Arsenal as an apprentice in 1961, with four years passing before he made his first-team debut, shortly after turning 20.

articles.title: Dan Campbell: Lions' Aidan Hutchinson Done For Year After Injury On Celebration
articles.summary: Aidan Hutchinson's sack celebration in the first quarter of the Detroit Lions' win over the New England Patriots quickly turned into great concern. And now, the Lions will have to make do without one of their top players for the rest of the year.
body: Lions head coach Dan Campbell confirmed in a press conference on Tuesday morning that Hutchinson suffered a torn ACL, which will require surgery and end the star defensive end's 2026 season.

Campbell told reporters after the game Sunday that the team would know more about Hutchinson's injury when they returned home from Germany, but the Lions already feared the injury would keep Hutchinson sidelined for the rest of the season, according to FOX Sports NFL Insider Jay Glazer.
Hutchinson's right knee appeared to buckle on the celebration, and he went down instantly. He was grabbing his right leg and needed assistance to get off the field following the sack.
Hutchinson was evaluated in the blue medical tent. A few moments later, he was seen walking gingerly back into the Lions' locker room and was later ruled questionable to return with a knee injury.
